sentences.sentence: **Don't I Know You**
As the fourth and final song faded, the DJ in our club at the north end of Waikiki kept the crowd pumped for another set of nude women on stage under the flashing black lights.
These men were mostly military dudes who were barely legal, lapping up the scene like it was their last tour abroad.
The DJ's eyes scanned the sea of sweaty, dancing bodies on the dancefloor and scanned their faces, searching for that spark, that look of 'don't I know you' in their eyes.
But as he scanned the sea of sweaty faces, he realized that everyone's eyes looked vaguely familiar, yet they all seemed so foreign, so distant.
Like they were mere shadows of people, echoes of people, echoes of a memory.
And as he gazed deeper, he felt a creeping sense of unease, a creeping sense of disconnection.
Like these people weren't really here, they were just projections, mere silhouettes in the flashing lights.
As the DJ's gaze wandered across the crowded dance floor, he saw a vision of a time long past, a time he thought was left behind.
A time of late night beach party, beneath the flashing palm trees, with the waves crashing in the background.
The DJ's heart started beating fast, as memories flooded back.
Memories of laughter, of laughter and music, of freedom and the ocean, of youth and the night.
And for a moment, the DJ was transported, taken away to a time that's lost, but not forgotten.

The flashing lights of the club, the pulsating music, the sweaty bodies, all faded away, and the DJ was back on that beach, on that night, with the waves crashing in the background, and the laughter and music and the youth.

sentences.sentence: The #1 Thing That Gets Me Through Difficult Days
My Coping Mechanism in Trying Times
Photo by Ian Chen on Unsplash
I remember the first few hours after my mother took her last breath.
The weight of her absence settled in, like a dense fog rolling in, enveloping me in a heavy, oppressive shroud.
I felt lost, alone, and helpless.
But, amidst the darkness and the grief, I had my journals.
They were my sanctuary, my safe haven, my lifeline.
I wrote down every thought, every feeling, every shred of emotion that bubbled to the surface.
I poured out my heart onto the page.
I also remember the first few days, when the reality of her being gone, hit me like a ton of bricks.
The overwhelming grief, the sadness, the loneliness, the numbness.
It was all overwhelming.
But, amidst the overwhelming grief, amidst the devastation, I sat with my journal, and I wrote.
I poured out all my emotions onto the pages.
I journaled my way through the first few days, the first few weeks, the first few months.
I journaled my way through the darkest, hardest, and most unimaginable days.
Writing was my sanctuary, my safe haven, my lifeline.
It was where I poured my heart out, where I released my emotions, where I processed my grief.
It was my coping mechanism, my savior, my therapy.
And, it still is.
To this day, I still journal, and I still find comfort in the act of writing.
For those who may not know, journaling is a powerful coping mechanism.
It's a way to release your emotions, to process your emotions, and to gain clarity.
It's a way to clear your mind, to calm your heart, and to ease your soul.
Journaling is a therapeutic outlet, a creative outlet, and a healing outlet.

sentences.sentence: **What's Shaking Up the Hospitality Industry?
A Call to Action for Hotels, Restaurants, and Resorts**
**How Prepared Are You for the Revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food, and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making waves and succeeding in the industry.
The formula looked a little something like this: build a beautiful building, hire competent staff, serve decent food, charge a decent price, and voila!
Patrons will flock to your doorstep.
Easy peasy, right?
Unfortunately, that formula is a relic of the past.
The hospitality landscape has dramatically changed and continues to change at a pace that's shaking the industry to its core.
From guest's expectations evolving to technology's rapid advancement, to shifting consumer's behaviors and the rise of the online-driven market.
Today's savvy travelers, diners and consumers are no longer content with "good enough".
They demand exceptional, and they demand it now, or else they'll move on to the next option.
So, what's shaking up the hospitality industry?
**Shifting Consumer's Expectations and Newfound Transparency**
Today's savvy, tech savvy and empowered consumers are no longer content with mediocrocracies.
They're no longer willing to settle for subpar service, subpar food, or subpar accommodations.
They're informed, vocal, and demanding.
With social media at their fingertips, they can instantaneously share their dining, hotel, and hospitality experience with the world.
And, be warned, their reviews can either make or break a business.
Transparency is the new "buzz" word.
Guests are demanding to know everything, and I mean, everything.
From what's in your food, to where's the bathroom, to what's the menu of the day.
They're craving authenticity, and authenticity is the new luxury.

Welcome to my little corner of the world, where life's rollercoasters of twists and turns will be shared with honesty, vulnerability, and authenticity.
I'm Liz, a 38-year-old mom, wife, and blogger who loves to share my stories, struggles, and triumphs with the world.

We might, at first, want to, 'hit the pause' button, but, life's momentum, keeps on moving, and, if we're lucky, we'll find the strength, the courage, to face it, head-on, and, learn from it.

sentences.sentence: **My Ego Sabotaged My Writing**
Illustration by [Fresh Idea]
Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the end of June, just a few weeks away.

I had been eager to attend this conference, it was one of the biggest in the industry and I was excited to network with fellow writers and industry professionals, but more importantly, to get feedback on my work.

I've been working on my novel for a while, and I've been seeking feedback from fellow writers, but the conference was going to be the perfect opportunity to get constructive, industry-professional feedback.
I know my writing has flaws, no one's perfect, and I was eager to hear, not just where I was going wrong, but how to improve, concrete, actionable, advice.
So, I made a goal, to have a manuscript in two months, and I thought, "piece of cake," I'm a seasoned pro, I've got this, I'll whip this baby into shape, no problem.
However, my ego, not I, stepped up to the plate.
Ego, the perpetual saboteur of dreams, goals, and creative endeavors.
It's been sitting in the wings, waiting to pounce, waiting to sabotage, and it did.
It whispered in my ear, "You're not going to make it, you'll never meet the deadline, you'll fail."
I stalled big time.
I didn't even begin, not seriously, that is.
I toyed with a few ideas, I jotted down a few notes, but I didn't do any real writing.
I didn't sit down and tackle this looming deadline like I should've.
And, now, it's too late.

sentences.sentence: I woke up as a different person today.
I am an altogether different person this year.
But I still feel like the 13 year old me is watching me over.
I remember how she never wanted to grow up, thinking she'll lose the carefree, spontaneous, and innocent spark that came with being young.
She longed to stay frozen in this carefree bubble forever, savoring every moment, never wanting to say goodbye to the beauty of childhood.
And yet, here we are, marking a crucial milestone in Sidra's journey.
Today, we celebrate Sidra's 18th birthday.
Becoming an adult is a bittersweet milestone.
It's a rite of passage, but it's also a departure from the simplicity of youth.
As we step into adulthood, we lose some of that carefree, spontaneous, and innocent spark that came with being young.
We start to worry, we start to care, and we start to lose sight of the beauty in every moment.
But amidst the midst of growing up and losing that spark, I'm grateful that the 13-year-old me is still watching over Sidra.
Her wisdom, her energy, and her spark remind us to never lose sight of the beauty in simplicity, to never lose sight of the beauty in every moment.
As we celebrate Sidra's 18th birthday, I want to remind her that it's okay to still see the world with the eyes of a 13-year-old.
It's okay to still believe in magic, to still feel the sun's warmth on your skin, and to still feel the grass beneath your feet.
Don't let growing up take that away from you, Sidra.
Hold on to the spark, hold on to the energy, and hold on to the innocence.
Celebrate this milestone, but don't be afraid to still be that 13-year-old at heart.

This is an invaluable resource, not just for those who miss Sunday, but for all of us, to deepen our walk with Christ.

The application questions that our leaders have included, with each Sunday's message, are a key part of what makes Vision 2020: The Well so valuable.
They provide us with practical and tangible ways to apply what we've learned, to our daily lives.
We're not just passively sitting in a pew, absorbing information, but we're actively engaging with our faith, and applying what we've learned, to our lives.

Not only is Vision 2020: The Well a great resource for personal application and growth, but it's also a great way to connect with others in our church community.
We're encouraged to discuss the Sunday's message, with a small group, or a friend, and this builds friendships, and strengthens our community ties.
This is an amazing opportunity to be encouraged, and to uplift, others, as we share our experiences, of applying what we've learned.

sentences.sentence: Photo by Harry Knight on Unsplash
“Card games, now that's a good way to pass the time."
An older woman observes my group of 15 high school students huddled in circles, playing games.
We've just spent a week in the great outdoors, unplugged, and disconnected from our devices.
No screens, no games, no social media.
Just us, the wilderness, and the moment.
As we sit by the campfire, surrounded by towering trees and the sound of the wind rustling through the leaves, I notice an older woman standing nearby, observing us with a nostalgic smile.
She's a grandmother, probably one of those 'old-school' types who grew up in a world without smartphones, tablets, or iPads.
And as she sees us laughing, giggling, and enjoying ourselves without a care in the world, she smiles.
“Card games, now that's a good way to pass the time,” she says, her voice dripping with nostalgia and longing.
And I know exactly what she's thinking.
She's thinking about a world long gone, a world where kids didn't need a phone to entertain them, where kids were happy to just be present, to just be.

And as I sit there, surrounded by my friends, the crunch of the bonfire's flames, the chirping of the crickets, the sound of the wind rustling through the leaves, and the smell of the wood, I'm reminded of something.
I'm reminded of the countless hours, we've wasted, stuck in front of screens, playing games, scrolling through social media, staring blankly, into a void.

We've let our addiction, to the internet, consume us, and in doing so, we've lost ourselves, we've lost our sense of wonder, our sense of awe, our sense of curiosity, our sense of excitement, and our sense of joy.

sentences.sentence: **Small Tweaks, Big Impact: Simple Changes That Helped Me Lose 5 Kg and Feel Great in Just One Month
Image by biscotto87
When the pandemic-induced lock down happened, I lost all motivation.
My lifestyle became sedentary, and I turned into a couch potato.
Up until then, I had maintained a regular fitness regime, hit the gym 4-5 times a week, and my diet was relatively balanced with a mix of Mediterranean and healthy portion control.
However, once the lockdown started, I stopped going to the gym and my diet became super irregular.
I woke up one day, weighed myself, and I was 85 kg.
I felt miserable.
The excess weight I had gained during the pandemic was starting to take a toll on my health and confidence.
So, I made a decision that I was going to lose that 5 Kg in 30 days, come hell or high water.
And I'm glad I took that decision.
I started with small tweaks, simple tweaks.
No drastic changes were made.
Just a few tweaks here and there.
I began to wake up 30 minutes earlier every day.
That extra 30 minutes was crucial.
I started walking 10,000 steps a day, every day.
And when I had breakfast, I started incorporating some protein powder in my breakfast, alongside a fruit.
And when it came to meals, I opted for smaller portions, of all food.
No seconds, no overeating.
No excess sweets, and no sugary drinks.
The first 15 days, I barely saw any results, I was still the same weight.
But I kept going.

**Small Tweaks, Big Impact: Simple Changes That Helped Me Lose 5 Kg and Feel Great in Just One Month

Image by biscotto87

When the pandemic-induced lock down happened, I lost all motivation. My lifestyle became sedentary, and I turned into a couch potato. Up until then, I had maintained a regular fitness regime, hit the gym 4-5 times a week, and my diet was relatively balanced with a mix of Mediterranean and healthy portion control. However, once the lockdown started, I stopped going to the gym and my diet became super irregular.

I woke up one day, weighed myself, and I was 85 kg. I felt miserable. The excess weight I had gained during the pandemic was starting to take a toll on my health and confidence. So, I made a decision that I was going to lose that 5 Kg in 30 days, come hell or high water. And I'm glad I took that decision.

I started with small tweaks, simple tweaks. No drastic changes were made. Just a few tweaks here and there. I began to wake up 30 minutes earlier every day. That extra 30 minutes was crucial. I started walking 10,000 steps a day, every day. And when I had breakfast, I started incorporating some protein powder in my breakfast, alongside a fruit. And when it came to meals, I opted for smaller portions, of all food. No seconds, no overeating. No excess sweets, and no sugary drinks.

The first 15 days, I barely saw any results, I was still the same weight. But I kept going. And, slowly but surely, I began to notice the pounds melting off. My energy levels increased, and I was sleeping better, too. My skin even started to glow, and I looked better, too.

Now, I'm not saying, I lost 5 Kg, effortlessly, in 30 days. No, it wasn't.
